body: GOG Galaxy, GOG's official app, is the best way to play GOG games on PC, and it's been lacking Linux support ever since it arrived. But an official Linux version is reportedly in the works, even if we don't yet have a confirmed date. That is according to GamingOnLinux , which spoke to joint-CEO Krzysztof Papliński. Papliński said, "Linux continues to be one of the topics we hear the most about from our community, and we really appreciate the passion and patience of everyone who’s been asking about it." They continue, "Following the role we announced earlier this year, we now have the specialist on board and are actively exploring the best way to approach Linux support for GOG Galaxy. Now, you can still technically play GOG games on Linux even without the official app. For Linux-supported games, you can run GOG through the Heroic Games Launcher , which is also a great way to avoid using the Epic Games Store. title: Chinese company reportedly building its own DUV chipmaking machines, and that's a really big deal
summary: Meanwhile, the US still hopes to block ASML from selling and servicing similar machines in China.
body: A Chinese state-backed company has begun mass producing deep ultraviolet lithography machines, reports The Information . That's a big step towards China's semiconductor biz standing on its own two feet. It takes a complicated lithographic machine to produce a modern chip, and there are two main types: EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography) and DUV (Deep Ultraviolet Lithography). It's the older of the two, DUV, that a Chinese company is said to have figured out. These sorts of immersion machines are still used for modern computer chips, and today most are made by Dutch company ASML, which took over from the Japanese companies that dominated prior. Citing people familiar with the matter, The Information says the Chinese DUV machines are set to be delivered to customers this year . Customers including, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp., Hua Hong Semiconductor, and ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). Yeah, that same CXMT everyone is talking about due to surging memory costs. While this does challenge ASML for the sale of DUV machines in China, the machines are said to be lagging behind in performance and reliability. This news comes at a time when a plan to restrict sale…

title: Cringe '90s stoner icons Jay and Silent Bob are getting a cosy farming sim, but wait for it: you farm weed
summary: Jay and Silent Bob: Joint Venture looks like Wario Animal Crossing.
body: Jay and Silent Bob first appeared in the 1994 grunge film Clerks as eccentric weed dealers. Jay was the sweary, loquacious, long haired slacker, and Silent Bob was the silent, ruminative long haired slacker. They were cult figures in the '90s. Most of my teenage friends thought they were very funny, and Clerks is still a fun time capsule of the early '90s. But like a lot of '90s phenomena, Jay and Silent Bob quickly contorted into parody. They've spawned at least three standalone films, each more silly than the last. They also reliably feature in every one of Kevin Smith's View Asknewiverse films, from Clerks all the way through to Clerks 3, but also taking in Mallrats, Chasing Amy and Dogma, just to name a handful. More recently they've started getting their own videogames: Jay and Silent Bob Mall Brawl is a 2020 sidescrolling beat 'em up developed for NES but also ported to PC and consoles. In April, Atari published Jay and Silent Bob: Chronic Blunt Punch , which is also a sidescrolling beat 'em up but with a modern comic book presentation. There are also two Jay and Silent Boss phone games, and an in-development VR game, and they both cameoed in Black Ops 6. Talk about selling …

title: After leaving Epic Games last month, its former 'Unreal evangelist' is now building his own game engine
summary: Sjoerd De Jong aims to combat game development "stagnation" he says has emerged from Epic and Unity market dominance.
body: In June, Sjoerd De Jong—an Unreal Engine modder and map creator turned full-time specialist at Epic Games— announced that he was leaving the company after 12 years as a senior director and Unreal Engine "lead evangelist." In a cryptic departure message, he said the games industry was at a "pivotal point," and he's aiming to "work out how to adapt and excel" at addressing the changing needs of videogame development. We now have a clearer idea of De Jong's plans for navigating the games industry's future. In an interview with This Week in Videogames , De Jong revealed what he's tackling next: He's building a game engine of his own. De Jong's nascent game engine competitor is called the Immens Engine, and he's building it alongside a small team of co-founders that includes former Epic technical director Arjan Brussee. De Jong intends for Immens to serve as an alternative to the dominance of Unreal and Unity, whose market influence he said has led to a "stagnation" in game development for which challengers like Godot have only just recently started to emerge. title: Vatican scrambles to patch 'phishing goldmine' app promoted by the Pope: 'Prayer infrastructure on the framework you learn in week 2 of a Node.js bootcamp'
summary: Jesus Christ.
body: On January 20, 2019, Pope Francis delivered his weekly Angelus to St Peter's Square from a window in the Vatican's Apostolic Palace. In it, he enjoined the faithful to join him on the Church's then-new Click To Pray app—helpfully modelled by a nearby priest, wielding a tablet. Hundreds of thousands of people signed up in the years that followed. But maybe they shouldn't have, because it turns out the Click To Pray app was, until very recently, absolutely rife with info-leaking security holes. White-hat hacker BobDaHacker revealed in a July 24 blog post (via The Register ) that "The Pope's official app exposes 700,000+ user emails." The vulnerability has since been fixed, but it seems only after BobDaHacker went public with their investigation—inquiries made by the hacker and by journalists stretching back to January this year went unanswered. The vulnerability itself was pretty simple. When you sign up for Click To Pray, the site hands your user account an ID number. The first guy to sign up was one, the next was two, and so on, all the way into the hundreds of thousands. title: Micron's low power DRAM 'consumes approximately one-third the power of DDR5' in AI data center workloads, but I'm not sure that's good news
summary: Micron finds LPDDR5X can account for less than 7% of total system power.
body: AI's hunger for both power and memory, plus the resulting supply crisis of the latter, has led to many industry players engaging in a spot of creative problem solving. Case in point, Micron and Meta have collaborated on an experimental data centre roll out of low power DRAM. Micron has developed SOCAMM2 , a fresh form factor for LPDDR5X that is a "modular, serviceable module designed for servers." Testing used "Meta’s open-source DCPerf benchmark suite, which reflects production environments across a hyperscale fleet," and found that this low-power DRAM module "consumes approximately one-third the power of DDR5." According to Micron's white paper report , that accounts for under 7% of total system power. The white paper goes on to elaborate that LPDDR5X's "reduced operating voltage and advanced signalling allows bandwidth to scale without a corresponding rise in power consumption, resulting in better bandwidth-per-watt performance than conventional server memory." Basically, data centres can install more low power DRAM without also hiking up power-related operating costs. The AI industry potentially switching away from DDR5 may sound like good news in the short term for memory-sta…

title: Jensen Huang's first-ever post on X is in defense of open access to AI models, alongside Google, OpenAI, and Meta
summary: Many companies argue a bad guy with an open AI is best fought by a good guy with an open AI.
body: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang joined X last month, and recently made his first-ever post . As you could probably guess, it's about AI. He argues, alongside companies like Google, OpenAI, and Meta, that the US should not aim to restrict open models 'prematurely', as they're important for the growth of AI (among other things). Taking a quick step back, Open models are ones that give access to weights or even code to see how it runs and to allow users to modify them. These can be run locally and are customisable. Closed models are those that tend to be run by specific companies, accessed via the cloud and APIs, and keep all their weights hidden. Open models out of China, like DeepSeek, became a problem for American AI firms at the start of last year. They exploded onto the scene, offering similar services to the likes of OpenAI, but totally free and available locally. Just last week, the Trump administration was reportedly looking to ban Chinese AI models due to cybersecurity concerns. The battle between closed and open models is also partially a digital proxy war between American and non-American AI. Open models give access to anyone, and the US is hoping for AI dominance. Sharing how i…

body: On Monday, Chinese memory manufacturer CXMT made its initial public offering on Shanghai's STAR stock market. This debut was the biggest in Asia this year, raising $8.6 billion and seeing shares in the company surge by 466%. In terms of valuation, that places CXMT right at the top of China's stock market. CXMT's market capitalisation is now about $487.73 billion. Major player Tencent still outpaces it at a little over $500 billion, but that makes CXMT's stock market debut no less show-stealing. In fact, according to Reuters , the memory manufacturer is now a more valuable listed company than even the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. Even before this news, CXMT was already one to watch; the company's plans to massively ramp up DRAM manufacturing capacity in the midst of the RAMpocalypse has made its products an appealing option for a number of PC component makers . Furthermore, recent reports suggest that CXMT is planning to expand overseas into the US market at some point in the future. CXMT's rise may be far from unstoppable, though. According to that document, the price increase will be a percentage in the double digits, and presumably, that rise will only worsen the price of the devices that use the company's chips. One such device is Valve's Steam Frame , which rocks a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and is said to be launching soon. The Steam Frame is its new wireless VR headset, and one designed for game streaming. It uses a special dongle for foveated streaming, which delivers the parts you are looking at in higher quality, saving on bandwidth. Steam has said all three pieces of its hardware triumvirate (Steam Controller, Steam Machine, and Steam Frame) would launch by the end of Summer, which means we have around a month left before that self-imposed deadline. body: I've said it before and, in all likelihood, will say it again several more times: one of the best things about PC gaming is that modders can come in long after a game has been set aside by its developers, and proceed to clean up all the nagging bugs and imperfections that continue to linger. Konami's done a lot of work on the games since then, and they're in a good state, but there's always work to be done. That's why MGSHDFix 4.0.0 released over the weekend. It's a doozy. body: The flood of retail simulators on Steam is nothing new: the trend seemed to land with torrential force in late 2024. But it's fascinating, to me at least, how many of these things are still being released every week, and how many of them seem to actually reach an audience despite their rudimentary appearance. Last week, 14 retail sims were released on Steam. I'm being pretty picky with what I class a "retail sim" too. If it's an idle game with a retail or service industry theme, it's not included. If it's a horror game with a retail setting—and there are tons of these, including this week's Shift at Midnight—they're not included either. If it's a puzzle game with retail or service industry themes, like Nothing To Declare , I'm not including it. No, I'm talking about those unfailingly first-person retail sims that extremely prolific Polish publisher PlayWay seemed to spawn into existence, and which have been copied relentlessly since (including by PlayWay itself). title: If you miss the straightforward action RPGs of the past, try the generous demo for Darkstone Restoration
summary: Open a portal, we're going back.
body: Before action RPGs relied on seasonal ladders and DLC treadmills there was Darkstone, a 1999 hack and slash where you clicked on things until they died and liked it. It had some interesting ideas, like the companion mode that lets you switch between two player-characters, the other controlled by the CPU while you took the lead, but it remained true to the basics of a genre I got into precisely because it was basic. Now it's back, with a remaster in early access that improves the UI and controls (you can move characters with WASD now, or play with a controller), and the graphics (though I had to turn off volumetric fog and procedural grass for the sake of my poor framerate). It's got a demo too, which lets you make characters from any of its eight classes and explore the early-game dungeons, letting you play three of its quests, which are selected at random each time you start a new game. It's just nice to start up an action RPG without having to worry about which build I'm going to pursue, or look at a massive node full of future skill unlocks, or wonder if I should start a seasonal character or whether I'm missing out by not buying the latest DLC. Darkstone is just Darkstone, a g…

title: J.K. Simmons hasn't played Baldur's Gate 3 or any of his games, but he loves Portal 2: 'I could have done the feature film, or the play, or whatever'

body: In a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , prolific actor J.K. Simmons dove into his relationship with the games he's acted in. "He said, 'I'm about to kill you.' Okay, well, good luck with that." Host Josh Horowitz followed up by asking if Simmons enjoys playing games at all, and the answer was a firm no. "My hands don't work on those controllers," said Simmons. "I've tried⁠—my kids, of course, my twentysomething kids play them a lot. But even if he doesn't play, Simmons does have a firm favorite among all the games he's acted in. "It was Portal 2, for me," he said. "Just because it was such a hilarious script. title: How do you feel about AI videogame music?
summary: Does your music require the human touch?
body: Like it or loathe it—and for the record, I am firmly in the latter camp–generative AI has continued to seep into every aspect of game development. What felt like the odd shovelware AI thumbnail here or generated texture there has transformed into "developers" parading around entirely vibe-coded videogames as if it's something to be celebrated, rather than looked upon with sheer horror at the willing dismantling of human creativity and spirit. Critical Hit (Image credit: Future) Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle. While videogame music has still largely held off from falling to generative AI, that doesn't mean it's not happening. YouTube has already become plagued with so-called "rearrangements" of beloved videogame scores that are, unsurprisingly, concocted entirely by a LLM. Spotify has been under intense scrutiny for the immense flooding of AI music across the platform—as well as fielding accusations that it's been planting AI-generated music it owns in its official playlists as a way to pay real artists less money. summary: Videogame piracy.
body: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a game with a title that feels like it ought to have a colon or an em dash somewhere in there, is finally here and it's selling like whatever the nautical equivalent of hotcakes is. Hardtack, I guess. Not only did it sell 2 million copies in a single day , a recent financial report includes Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot saying "Two weeks in, the title has already exceeded the annual expectations we had." "The strong launch of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced in early July by Vantage Studios is an encouraging proof point," he said. "The game is the highest-rated Assassin's Creed title since the original Black Flag, and we are very pleased with the praise it received from players … I would like to warmly thank the teams whose talent and dedication brought it to life." Guillemot's thanks come at an interesting time, given that nearly a third of Ubisoft Barcelona was laid off just weeks ago, triggering a labor strike . This was part of a larger wave of layoffs which affected hundreds of workers. As it has done with a variety of Ubisoft games, Ubisoft Barcelona supported the development of Black Flag Resynced and "did all the underwater levels" as…
